Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T15:02:00Z
Subject: Recap + proposed POC plan (model selection items)

Hi Elena / Carlos,

Thanks again for the call today. Great to hear more about Novus AI's use case (multi-lingual summarization for customer support transcripts) and the volume/timing constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs
- Primary objective: achieve high-accuracy concise summaries (English + ES/PT) for support conversations with < 350ms median token latency on inference.
- Throughput: ~200 concurrent active sessions initially, spiky traffic up to 600 sessions during peak.
- Data: no PII to be sent to hosted model for the initial POC; Novus will use redacted transcripts stored in S3.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Quality: human eval A/B vs current baseline shows >= 10% improvement on F1/ROUGE metrics or equivalent qualitative score for 3 representative prompt sets.
2) Latency: 95th percentile per-turn latency < 800ms (target 500ms) on Dedicated config.
3) Cost: projected per-1M-token inference cost <= $X (we'll finalize after we size the batch/quant settings).
4) Stability: zero major errors (time-outs/OOM) during 72-hour soak test at target throughput.

Model selection questions from my side
- Preferred open models to test: Mistral-Instruct-7B (fast, good multilingual performance), Llama-2-Chat-13B (strong instruction-following baseline), Falcon-40B-Instruct (fallback for difficult long-context cases).
- Suggested primary candidate: Mistral-Instruct-7B quantized to 8-bit for the POC to balance latency/cost. Fallback: Llama-2-Chat-13B (if we need better instruction alignment) and Falcon-40B-Instruct only for long-context scenarios.
- Multilingual support: recommend running targeted eval sets in Spanish/Portuguese; if quality gaps show up, consider small-domain adapter tuning or few-shot prompt templates.

Proposed timeline / owners
- Week 0 (this week): sign MSA + mutual action plan (attached). Owner: Ben.
- Week 1: infra setup (dedicated test pool), data ingest & redaction script. Owner: Novus (Carlos) + Redwood SE (Marissa).
- Week 2: run initial evals against three models (Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B, Falcon-40B). Owner: Marissa.
- Week 3: soak test + human eval + cost analysis. Owner: Marissa + Ben.
- Week 4: review results and recommend production model + rollout plan. Owner: Ben + Novus Eng.

Attachments: I attached the Novus requirements PDF and a draft Mutual Action Plan (Excel) for timelines/owners.

Next steps (for this week)
- Elena/Carlos: confirm success criteria and whether we should include PT as priority language in the POC.
- Novus: Share a sample of redacted transcripts (S3 link) and confirm the max sequence length needed.
- Redwood: Marissa to prepare an initial evaluation harness and perf baseline.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min technical sync if helpful.

Thanks,

Hi all, jumping in from SE side with technical answers and a recommended evaluation plan. Thanks for the clear brief, Ben.

Model recommendation (short):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B quantized to 8-bit (best trade-off for latency/cost; we have prior evals showing solid ES coverage).
- Secondary/fallback: Llama-2-Chat-13B (better instruction alignment for corner cases).
- Long-context fallback: Falcon-40B-Instruct or a segmented-chunking approach if 3,000-token contexts are required; both options increase cost.

Why Mistral-7B first
- Latency: it consistently gives ~30-40% lower latency than 13B-sized chat models on our dedicated inference pool when quantized.
- Multilingual: performs well on Spanish benchmarks in our internal tests; PT is weaker but can be improved with prompt templates or a small adapter.

Evaluation plan (detailed):
1) Data prep: Novus shares 1,500 redacted examples (English+ES ~80/20 split) with labels for desired summary length and quality.
2) Automatic evals: ROUGE, BERTScore, and a custom token-level fidelity check.
3) Human evals: 5 bilingual raters across 300 sampled examples (50% ES) with scoring on accuracy, conciseness, and hallucination.
4) Perf tests: run throughput and latency tests on a dedicated 4xA100-equivalent pool; include 72-hour soak.
5) Cost modeling: run tokenized simulations on sample traffic to estimate monthly spend for each model/config.

Quantization & runtime notes
- We'll start with 8-bit quant (q8) and experiment with q4 if the accuracy drop is acceptable. q8 gives the best starting point for your latency targets.
- For PT gaps: propose a quick adapter training pass (200-300 steps) on Novus-labeled PT examples if human evals show a >15% quality delta vs EN/ES. This would be a small incremental cost.

Security / model weights
- For the Private deployment option: Redwood can arrange for model weights to be deployed into your VPC (no model weights are shared via third-party buckets). We'll document exact delivery method in the MSA appendix.

Next actions I will take
- Prepare the evaluation harness and perf scripts (ETA: 3 business days).
- Provide per-token cost estimates for Mistral-7B (q8) vs Llama-2-13B (q8) by tomorrow.

Ben, let me know when you've received the S3 samples and I'll queue the evals.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
